checks.criterion: 100 race-enabled repeats: lose first 12 size probes, answer controls; recover wire limit >=1392 within 35 virtual seconds; IPv6 QUIC Initial goes native
1357-byte and below-QUIC-floor paths never adopt a limit larger than the measured path; at most three recovery searches per association; no size probes after the budget is exhausted
Client increases limit only after exact generation+limit acknowledgement; lost, duplicate, reordered and stale acknowledgements cannot commit another proposal
RC2 client/RC1 server and RC1 client/RC2 server pass HTTPS+native UDP; old peers retain one-shot limit behavior and no recovery search
Normal native liveness intervals, loss thresholds, TCP fallback and healthy wide-path size-probe budget unchanged
No tracked agent instruction files; every tracked README is English; no local absolute links or working secrets in changed published files
Full scripts/pre-commit.sh passes with RC2 stamp; all release targets build; source/binary hashes recorded

Fixed-source raw/2.3/RC1/RC2 comparison on physical ARM router and WAN; >=5 repeats, quiet and same controlled background load; no content/connection errors; noisy measurements excluded from speed claims
Backups complete; server and router D client live hashes match tested RC2; HTTPS and UDP pass; unrelated configuration preserved; no new unexpected WARN/ERROR

Three real Discord sessions >=2h through D, each with confirmed outgoing speech, silence and usual Mihomo load, including a >=10min silence then speech. No outgoing voice outage or unexplained association loss; both-side timestamped evidence retained. Missing real-session evidence keeps this pending.
Private compressed snapshots of all three servers and router clients every five minutes; seven-day retention; passive read-only collection; notify only on new actionable failures/counter changes

Repeat the observed fallback/buffer-drop cases with per-socket or isolated-network-namespace counters and establish attribution; no unexplained candidate-only persistent outage. This remains open and prevents calling RC2 a fully accepted stable release.
